- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.2) or volatile, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish or uncertain sentiment.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast rise to 5–7% above prior day’s high.  
- In flat sentiment (sentiment ≈0.0), model shows strong mean-reversion bias; forecast should be adjusted toward historical mean or 30-day moving average.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from model’s first day prediction, check for lag: if true outcome is rising, model may be too early; if falling, model may be too late — adjust horizon sensitivity.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.0 values, model tends to overestimate mean; apply downward bias of 2–5% to forecast unless sentiment turns positive.
